title: Is Tua Tagovailoa still a good quarterback?
text:
Tua Tagovailoa has been the starting quarterback for the Miami Dolphins since 2020 when he replaced the former starting quarterback, Ryan Fitzpatrick, midway through the season. He showed great potential in the nine games he started that season, but he was still somewhat inconsistent. As he progressed into other seasons, Tagovailoa started to face injuries to his ribs and fingers that caused him to miss games in his second season. In his third season, he broke out of his shell. Head coach of the Dolphins, Mike McDaniel, started having the team play to Tagovailoa’s strengths, greatly improving the Dolphins’ offense. Tagovailoa is not invincible though. He suffered multiple concussions that ended his season early.  
The 2023 season was Tagovailoa’s best season. He managed to stay uninjured and was ranked the number one quarterback by multiple sources and led the league in passing yards for the season. As he entered the 2024 season, he looked strong and ready for the season but got yet another concussion resulting in him missing in weeks three through seven. With Tagovailoa’s consistent injury track record, many football fans are saying, “He should retire now because he’s not what he used to be.” Yes, he seems to be injury prone, but is he still a good quarterback? 
When comparing Tagovailoa’s completed passes to his touchdown passes over the past five seasons, he ranks somewhere in the middle among other quarterbacks. There also is not a clear trend of improvement or decline from season to season. His best season by far was 2023. He had 388 completed passes and 29 touchdowns. His 2024 season took a hit and declined to 291 completed passes and 19 touchdowns. This decline could be a result of him not playing from week three through seven. If Tagovailoa had played every game of the 2024 season, he may have been able to match or top his 2023 season. 


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggbump)
library(ggnewscale)
library(ggalt)
library(ggtext)
library(patchwork)
library(ggrepel)

quarterbacks <- read_csv("qbs19752024.csv")

qbs <- quarterbacks |> 
  filter(Season >= 2020, G >= 10) |>
  arrange(Player)


Tua <- qbs |>
  filter(Player == "Tua Tagovailoa") |>
   filter(
      Season >= 2022,
    Season <= 2024
  )

Tua2 <- qbs |>
  filter(Player == "Tua Tagovailoa")

tenathletes <- qbs |>
  filter(
    Player == "Lamar Jackson"|
    Player == "Josh Allen"|
    Player == "Joe Burrow"|
    Player == "Justin Herbert"|
    Player == "Trevor Lawrence"|
    Player == "Jared Goff"|
    Player == "Geno Smith"|
    Player == "Patrick Mahomes"|
    Player == "Jalen Hurts" |
    Player == "Tua Tagovailoa") |>
    filter(
      Season >= 2022,
    Season <= 2024
  )

qbranks <- qbs |> 
  filter(PassingYds > 1000) |> 
  group_by(Season) |> 
  arrange(desc(QBR)) |> 
  mutate(Rank = row_number()) |> 
  ungroup()

topqbranks <- qbranks |> filter(Player %in% tenathletes$Player)

ggplot() + 
  geom_point(
    data=qbs, aes(x=TD, y=Cmp),
    color="gray84") +
  geom_point(
    data=Tua2, 
    aes(x=TD, y=Cmp), 
    color="#008E97", size=3
    ) + 
  geom_text_repel(
    data=Tua2, 
    aes(x=TD, y=Cmp, label=Season)
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(x=5, y=50, label="Few Completions &\nFew Touchdowns"), color="red3") +
  geom_text(aes(x=40, y=460, label="Many Completions &\nMany Touchdowns"), color="green4") +
  labs(
    x="Touch Downs", 
    y="Completed Passes", 
    title="Tua appears average", 
    subtitle="The amount of Tua's touch downs compared to his completed \npasses falls right in the middle of the pack and shows no clear trend.", 
    caption="Source: Pro Football Reference | By Autumn Young"
    ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank())









Tua Tagovailoa appears to be on the lower end of the top quarterbacks when comparing each of their total completions over the last three seasons. Tagovailoa has a noticeably fewer number of completions in the 2022 and 2024 seasons. This makes his total completions appear a lot worse than what they are. It is important to remember that he is prone to injuries and tends to miss some games. This is a large contributing factor to his fewer completions over those seasons, but it is impressive that even with his setbacks he still is ranked among other top quarterbacks. 


Code
bar1 <- ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=tenathletes, aes(x=reorder(Player, Cmp), weight=Cmp, fill=factor(Season))) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("grey91","grey77","grey47"), name="Seasons") +
  new_scale_fill() +
  geom_bar(data=Tua, aes(x=reorder(Player, Cmp), weight=Cmp, fill=factor(Season))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#008E97","#FC4C02","#005778"), name="") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x="", 
    y="Completed Passes") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

bar2 <- ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=tenathletes, aes(x=reorder(Player, `Cmp%`), weight=`Cmp%`, fill=factor(Season))) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("grey91","grey77","grey47"), name="Seasons") +
  new_scale_fill() +
  geom_bar(data=Tua, aes(x=reorder(Player, `Cmp%`), weight=`Cmp%`, fill=factor(Season))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#008E97","#FC4C02","#005778"), name="") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x="", 
    y="Completion Percentage") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  

bar1 / bar2  + 
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Fewer completions but still accurate",
    subtitle = "Tua saw fewer completions than other quarterbacks in the last three years, but he comes out on top for accuracy.",
    caption = "Source: Pro Football Reference | By Autumn Young"
  ) & 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )









Even with his fewer total completions over the past three seasons, Tua Tagovailoa has the highest completion percentage when compared to those same quarterbacks. This proves that while he has had less chances to throw the ball, he made the most of when he did throw it. His throws are more accurate than other quarterbacks such as Patrick Mahomes who had the most total completions over the last three seasons.  
Debatably one of the most important things to consider when trying to figure out if Tua Tagovailoa is still a good quarterback is his quarterback rating (QBR). In the beginning of his professional career, Tagovailoa had a very average QBR. He did show potential and was not too far behind some of the other up and coming quarterbacks. From 2020 through 2022 there is a steady increase in his QBR, and he peaked in 2022 with a 70.6 QBR. He had the third highest QBR that season and was only beaten by Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen. 


Code
ggplot() + 
  geom_bump(data = topqbranks, aes(x=Season, y=QBR, color=Player)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("grey", "grey", "grey", "grey", "grey", "grey", "grey", "grey", "grey", "grey")) +
  geom_bump(data = Tua2, aes(x=Season, y=QBR), color="#008E97") +
  geom_point(data=topqbranks, aes(x=Season, y=QBR, color=Player), size = 4) +
  geom_point(data=Tua2, aes(x=Season, y=QBR), color="#008E97", size = 4) +
  geom_text(data = topqbranks |> filter(Season == min(Season)), aes(x = Season - .2, y=QBR, label = ""), size = 3, hjust = 1) +
  geom_text(data = topqbranks |> filter(Season == max(Season)), aes(x = Season + .2, y=QBR, label = ""), size = 3, hjust = 0) +
   scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,80)) +
  labs(
    title="Change in QBR over the seasons",
    subtitle="<span style = 'color:#008E97;'>Tua Tagovailoa's</span> quarterback rating was on the rise in his early career, but has fallen and plateaued to average \nstatus in recent seasons.",
    y= "Quarterback Rating",
    x = "",
    caption="Source: Pro Football Reference | By Autumn Young") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle = element_textbox_simple(), element_text(size=10), 
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) 









After the 2022 season Tagovailoa’s QBR fell to 60.8 which seems dramatic but actually is not horrible. There was not much change from 2022 to 2023 as his QBR dropped to 60.3. That is hardly a noticeable difference. These quarterback ratings still keep him in the top 50% of quarterbacks currently in the league. In the 2023 season, he was still in the top 10. 
It is hard to answer the question, “Is Tua Tagovailoa still a good quarterback?” While his season statistics are not looking horrible, his QBR is potentially in danger. Overall, it will be hard to tell if he is still good or not until he has more seasons without injuries that impact the number of games he plays. Tagovailoa could definitely have a few more good seasons in him though.
